from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Hash functions take input to fixed-length strings.",
            "They are one-way streets, impossible to reverse.",
            "Changing input triggers the avalanche effect."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Digital Fingerprint: Hash Functions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        input_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color="#FFFFFF").set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        input_label = Text("Data Input", font_size=18)
        input_group = VGroup(input_box, input_label)
        
        hash_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFD700").set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.3)
        hash_label = Text("SHA-256", font_size=16)
        hash_group = VGroup(hash_circle, hash_label)
        
        output_box = Rectangle(width=3, height=0.5, color="#00FF00").set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        output_label = Text("Hash Output", font_size=18)
        output_group = VGroup(output_box, output_label)
        
        # Positioning
        self.place_at_grid(input_group, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(hash_group, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(output_group, 'D2')
        
        arrow1 = Arrow(input_group.get_right(), hash_group.get_left(), buff=0.1)
        arrow2 = Arrow(hash_group.get_right(), output_group.get_left(), buff=0.1)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(input_group), Create(hash_group), Create(arrow1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(output_group), Create(arrow2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        output_text = Text("a1b2c3d4...", font_size=20, color=WHITE).move_to(output_box)
        self.play(Write(output_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Digital Signatures: Asymmetric Cryptography", [
            "Public-Key Infrastructure uses a key pair system.",
            "Private key signs, public key verifies.",
            "Math allows verification without revealing the secret."
        ])
        
        # Define elements
        priv_key = Text("Private Key", color=BLUE)
        pub_key = Text("Public Key", color=YELLOW)
        doc = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=0.6, color=WHITE)
        sig = Text("Signature", font_size=20, color=PURPLE)
        check = Tex(r"$\checkmark$", color=GREEN, font_size=60)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(priv_key, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(pub_key, "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(priv_key), FadeIn(pub_key))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(doc, "D2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(doc))
        self.play(doc.animate.move_to(self.grid["C2"]))
        self.play(Write(sig))
        self.place_at_grid(sig, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(sig.animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]))
        self.play(FadeIn(check))
        self.place_at_grid(check, "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(check.animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Proof of Work: The Mathematical Lottery", 
                          ["Miners race to find a random nonce.", 
                           "The hash must start with specific zeros.", 
                           "Success is instantly verifiable by the network."])
        
        # Elements
        tx_list = Text("Transactions", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        mining_icon = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=0.5)
        mining_text = Text("Mining", font_size=20, color="#FFD700")
        mining_group = VGroup(mining_icon, mining_text)
        
        nonce_val = Text("Nonce: 12345", font_size=24, color="#ADD8E6")
        hash_result = Text("Hash: 0000a1b2...", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        
        block_header = VGroup(
            Text("Block Header", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            nonce_val,
            hash_result
        ).arrange(DOWN)
        
        reward = Text("Reward Received!", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(tx_list, "B2")
        self.play(Write(tx_list))
        self.place_at_grid(mining_group, "C2")
        self.play(Create(mining_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(block_header, "D4")
        self.play(FadeIn(block_header))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(reward, "E4")
        self.play(Write(reward), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Blocks link via the previous block's hash.", "Altering one block invalidates the entire chain.", "This ensures security through mathematical immutability."]
        self.setup_layout("The Immutable Chain: Blockchain Integration", lecture_lines)
        
        # Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg
        block_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg"
        
        blocks = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            block = SVGMobject(block_path, color=WHITE)
            block.set_stroke(WHITE, width=2)
            blocks.add(block)
        
        self.place_at_grid(blocks[0], 'C2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(blocks[1], 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(blocks[2], 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        arrows = VGroup()
        for i in range(2):
            arrow = Arrow(start=blocks[i].get_right(), end=blocks[i+1].get_left(), buff=0.1, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
            arrows.add(arrow)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(blocks[0]), FadeIn(blocks[1]), FadeIn(arrows[0]))
        self.play(FadeIn(blocks[2]), FadeIn(arrows[1]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        
        # Highlight: Altering blocks turns everything RED
        self.play(
            blocks.animate.set_color(RED),
            arrows.animate.set_color(RED)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Highlighting the hash link in green
        self.play(arrows.animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Mathematical Foundations of Bitcoin: Trust through Cryptography
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of algebra and computer logic.

sections.title: The Digital Fingerprint: Hash Functions (1 min)
sections.content: Introduce Cryptographic Hash Functions (SHA-256). Explain that a hash function takes any input and turns it into a fixed-length string of characters. Key concept: It is a 'one-way' street—easy to calculate but impossible to reverse.
sections.example: Visualize a digital meat grinder: If you put a cat in, you get a unique 64-character code. If you change even one whisker on the cat, the code changes entirely, illustrating the 'avalanche effect'.

sections.title: Digital Signatures: Asymmetric Cryptography (1.5 min)
sections.content: Explain Public-Key Infrastructure (PKI). Introduce the concept of a Key Pair: a Private Key (your digital secret) and a Public Key (your digital address). Math concept: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) creates a relationship where the public key can verify the private key without revealing it.
sections.example: Imagine a magical lockbox: You give out millions of copies of your open padlock (Public Key). When you use your secret key (Private Key) to sign a message, anyone with the padlock can verify it was you, but they can't open your vault.

sections.title: Proof of Work: The Mathematical Lottery (1.5 min)
sections.content: Explain how Bitcoin miners compete. They must find a 'nonce' (a random number) that, when hashed with transaction data, produces a result starting with a specific number of zeros. It’s a computationally expensive trial-and-error game.
sections.example: Imagine a forest of robotic squirrels. The network sets a rule: 'Find a nut that makes the scale weigh exactly 5 grams.' Thousands of squirrels race to try different nuts. The first one to succeed announces it, and the others verify it instantly.

sections.title: The Immutable Chain: Blockchain Integration (1 min)
sections.content: Synthesize the previous concepts. Explain how each block contains the hash of the *previous* block. This creates a mathematical link where altering one block invalidates the entire chain, ensuring global security.
sections.example: Visualize a stack of LEGO bricks where each new brick contains a tiny picture of the previous one. If you try to swap an old brick, the 'picture' inside the next one no longer matches, and the whole tower turns red, signaling a tamper attempt.
